transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-24
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Morris (BrightBridge), Diego Ramos (BrightBridge), Priya Nair (BrightBridge), Sam (BrightBridge)

Summary (auto): quick review of last week's runs, adjusted batching and concurrency, identified queuing at 32+ concurrent requests, next run to test higher concurrency with adjusted queue size and batching window.

[00:00] Maya: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to go over the throughput runs from last week and action on tuning continuous batching and queueing, make sure that aligns with you all
[00:18] Lena: yep thanks, we saw the spreadsheet, uh some of the numbers looked promising at 16 concurrency but then tail latency spiked at 32, so curious what you changed
[00:33] Arjun: yeah so quick context, we increased the batching window from 8ms to 20ms to allow more continuous batching on the GPU side, that improved token/sec at steady-state but introduced burst queuing when concurrency went above 24
[00:48] Diego: right we observed CPU on the host node bumping and kube kube-scheduler seemed to delay some pods, so it might be infra too, not just model serving
[01:05] Priya: and we also saw some KV cache misses which I think contributed to extra generation time for repeated prompts
[01:20] Maya: okay good, so items to cover: batch window, max queue length, concurrency targets and fallback policy. Arjun can you walk through the run results?
[01:34] Arjun: sure yes, so I posted the runs in the sheet - link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/BB-POC (note: internal link) - run A was concurrency 8, window 8ms, run B concurrency 16 window 20ms, run C 32 window 20ms, run D 64 window 20ms. p50/p95/p99 latencies are in column F-H
[01:58] Speaker 5: I think speaker 5 is us, the p95 at 32 jumped because queue depth caused some cold starts? or because of CPU?
[02:12] Arjun: partially both, we saw the runtime trigger more kernel swaps at higher seq lengths, and host CPU contention delayed batching flushes so queues accumulated
[02:26] Lena: can you explain kernel swaps? I'm not 100% on that terminology
[02:31] Arjun: sure, on some GPUs the runtime chooses different attention kernels depending on sequence length and batch size; when the runtime switches it can temporarily increase GPU scheduling overhead, which in high-concurrency scenarios amplifies latency
[02:47] Diego: and from infra we had container restarts for two pods during run D which didn't fully drain because our kube-probes are aggressive, so that added to tail latency
[03:01] Maya: okay so multi-factor - infra, runtime kernel behavior, and KV cache misses. For this week the plan we proposed was to test three things: bump the continuous batching window, increase max queue size slightly, and run with pinned model variant (quantized) to reduce kernel swap variability
[03:22] Priya: quick question on pinned model variant - if we pin the quantized variant does that affect quality? we have clinical text so we can't have hallucinations increase
[03:32] Arjun: good point, quantization can affect quality slightly but our evals on your dev prompt set showed negligible regression at 8-bit-quant. we'll include the regression run in the benchmarks, so you'll see rouge/accuracy numbers alongside latency
[03:46] Lena: ok good to hear, we need that documented for compliance review too
[03:51] Maya: noted, I'll attach the evaluation table. Alright Arjun, what were the specific queue settings you recommend?
[03:59] Arjun: right - current POC config used max_queue=200, we saw queuing above 150 cause p95 spikes; recommendation: lower to 120 for fairness and increase batching window to 30ms for the long-tail run, and run concurrency targets 8/16/32/64 to map the knee of the curve
[04:18] Diego: lowering queue to 120 might cause rejects at peaks, can we implement backpressure instead of rejects?
[04:25] Arjun: yes Redwood runtime supports graceful backpressure - we can route overload to a warm fallback variant with slightly lower perf or return 429s depending on policy. For the POC we'll enable soft backpressure: queueing until max, then shed to a lower-cost variant for non-critical requests
[04:44] Sam: are those fallback variants quantized too?
[04:48] Arjun: yes generally fallback will be a quantized variant or a smaller model/embedding-based reranker depending on latency target
[04:54] Speaker 2: small note, the cloud region we used had burstable vCPU; for fairness we should pin to a dedicated instance type for the long run
[05:04] Diego: agreed, I'll spin up dedicated instances for the next run - I can mirror the pod sizing we used earlier but with reserved CPU so we avoid noisy neighbor effects
[05:15] Lena: timeline - when can we get the longer run?
[05:18] Maya: Arjun?
[05:20] Arjun: I can run it tomorrow night; it's a one-hour run per concurrency point so roughly 4 hours total to complete all points, then I'll upload results and a short write-up
[05:33] Priya: good. Also on monitoring - can we get per-token cost breakdowns? we want to estimate monthly run cost if we scale to prod
[05:42] Maya: yes Redwood Console sample breakdown will show token cost, GPU minutes, and amortized model warmup costs; I'll include a sample export
[05:50] Speaker 3: we should also schedule a deep technical session on kernel-level behavior, maybe bring in someone from runtime team
[05:57] Arjun: I can bring in Lina (runtime engineer) for that deep-dive next week if you want
[06:02] Lena: that would be great, yes please
[06:06] Maya: ok Lina for deep-dive, Arjun for runs, Diego for infra, Lena and Priya to validate results and compliance notes. Any red flags on security? they asked earlier about SSO and audit logs
[06:18] Priya: we need SOC2 type II and audit logs for data access, also KMS integration for encryption at rest - does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[06:28] Maya: yes we support KMS/HSM integration on Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we have encryption at rest but can provide a managed key option for enterprise. I'll attach the security docs and a SOC2 summary
[06:39] Sam: perfect. Back to tuning, one more question - how does continuous batching interact with prompt caching? if many prompts are identical we should benefit from prefix cache right?
[06:51] Arjun: correct - prefix/KV cache reduces per-token compute for repeated sequences; we saw ~20% CPU/GPU savings on runs with a high repeat ratio. We recommend pre-warming cache for heavy repetitive traffic
[07:05] Diego: can the cache be shared across model variants?
[07:08] Arjun: cache is variant-specific because kv cache layout differs slightly, but for similar quantized variants the cache hit rate still helps; we'll include a cache-warmup script in the repo we share
[07:19] Lena: about cost - what about batching window tradeoff, if we increase window to 30ms we add latency but reduce token/sec cost, is there a sweet spot?
[07:32] Maya: yes it's always a tradeoff, the idea is to find the knee where cost per token improves faster than latency degrades beyond your SLO. We'll surface cost/latency curves so you can pick operation point
[07:45] Arjun: and we can do weighted routing by customer tier if you want different SLOs for internal vs external traffic
[07:53] Priya: that could help. For now we aim for p95 under 800ms and p50 under 200ms - those are rough targets from product
[08:03] Arjun: noted, we'll flag runs that breach p95>800ms as failures for the POC gating
[08:10] Maya: quick note on benchmarking methodology - Arjun, include 95% confidence intervals and note any pod restarts or infra events in the sheet
[08:18] Arjun: will do
[08:20] Speaker 4: someone mentioned earlier quantization - can you remind us what levels you tested?
[08:24] Arjun: we tested int8 (8-bit) and 4-bit where feasible; 4-bit gave better token/sec but slightly more variance in some prompts, so we recommend int8 for stability in this POC
[08:36] Diego: do we need to change container runtime flags for pinned kernel behavior?
[08:40] Arjun: small flags, yes - I'll paste them in the sheet under run config. It's basically RT scheduling tweak and a runtime env var for kernel preference
[08:49] Lena: ok, compliance wants to see an explicit list of changes to infra config before we touch production - we'll need that doc
[08:57] Maya: I'll prepare a short change doc and attach to the next meeting notes
[09:02] Sam: any blockers for the next run?
[09:05] Diego: infra will provision dedicated instances tonight; I just need the exact pod specs from Arjun
[09:09] Arjun: sending pod spec after call
[09:12] Maya: perfect. Any other questions?
[09:15] Priya: not from me, just to confirm the next meeting cadence - same time next week?
[09:20] Maya: yes same time, and we'll do a deeper runtime deep-dive mid-week if Lina is available
[09:25] Lena: sounds good. Thanks everyone
[09:28] Maya: recap of next steps: Arjun runs 4 concurrency runs (8/16/32/64) with window 30ms / queue 120 on dedicated instances, include p50/p95/p99 and cost breakdown; Lena provisions dataset; Maya shares pricing and security docs; schedule runtime deep-dive with Lina.
[09:49] Maya: I'll drop the benchmark link and the addendum into the CRM note and Slack channel after this call
[10:00] (meeting ends)
